Why Your Nose Gets Raw When You're Sick, and How Doctors Recommend Preventing It

Understanding Cold-Season Nasal Irritation

Fewer things make cold season quite as miserable as a nose that is red, raw, and sore. Between chilly outdoor air, dry indoor heating, and the constant friction of nose blowing, the delicate skin around the nostrils and the sensitive lining inside the nose can quickly become dry, cracked, and tender. For many people, this results in flaking skin, painful sores, or even minor nosebleeds.

To understand why this happens and how to manage it, medical professionals emphasize that much of the discomfort stems from the body's immune response. According to ear, nose, and throat (ENT) specialists, catching a cold triggers white blood cells to cause swelling and inflammation in the nasal tissues as they fight off the virus.

The Role of Inflammation and Friction

When cold viruses enter the nasal passages, immune cells release specific messengers that dilate blood vessels and increase mucus production to trap pathogen particles. While this is a normal part of healing, the resulting swelling and excess mucus create secondary physical challenges.

Increased mucus production inevitably leads to frequent wiping and blowing. According to Dr. Madeleine Herman, an ENT physician and president of the Sinus Center and ENT Specialists of Houston, this mechanical friction irritates the delicate skin and lining of the nose, including the septum. Combined with dry indoor heating, the tissue easily becomes compromised.

Expert Prevention and Soothing Strategies

Medical experts suggest several straightforward habits to protect nasal tissue during an illness:

  • Prioritize Moisture: Using a bedside humidifier overnight counteracts dry indoor air, while staying well-hydrated helps maintain moisture levels throughout the body.
  • Gentle Techniques: Doctors advise blowing the nose gently rather than aggressively or repeatedly wiping, which strips the skin's barrier.
  • Saline and Ointments: Simple saline nasal sprays can help clear and moisten nasal passages without harsh chemicals, while protective barrier ointments applied around the nostrils can shield raw skin from further friction.
